text: In the definition of an elementary topos, the exponential (function object) $B^A$ is characterized as the right adjoint to which functor?
explanation: The chapter defines exponentials as 'the function object $B^A$ (right adjoint to $-\times A$),' i.e. $\mathrm{Hom}(C\times A,B)\cong\mathrm{Hom}(C,B^A)$. The diagonal functor's right adjoint is the product, not the exponential; pullback functors appear in the chapter only as the maps that preserve finite limits; and a general topos need not have a forgetful functor to $\mathbf{Set}$.
